_meta.indication: QUVIVIQ is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with insomnia, characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, fixed-dose, 1:1:1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing daridorexant 25 mg and 50 mg to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and elderly subjects with insomnia disorder according to DSM-5 criteria
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: 2-night mean WASO and LPS change from baseline to Month 1 and Month 3
pivotal_trials.n: 930 randomized; 310 daridorexant 25 mg, 308 daridorexant 50 mg, 309 placebo (safety population)
pivotal_trials.result: Daridorexant 50 mg vs placebo: WASO treatment effect -22.78 min at Month 1 and -18.30 min at Month 3 (both p<0.0001); LPS treatment effect -11.35 min at Month 1 (p=0.0000) and -11.67 min at Month 3 (p=0.0000)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, fixed-dose, 1:1:1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing daridorexant 10 mg and 25 mg to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and elderly subjects with insomnia disorder according to DSM-5 criteria
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: 2-night mean WASO and LPS change from baseline to Month 1 and Month 3
pivotal_trials.n: 924 randomized; 306 daridorexant 10 mg, 308 daridorexant 25 mg, 306 placebo (safety population)
pivotal_trials.result: Daridorexant 25 mg met WASO (12-minute improvement vs placebo at Month 1 and 10-minute improvement at Month 3) but did not reject the null for LPS (LPS 25 mg treatment effect -6.45 min at Month 1, p=0.0302, and -9.01 min at Month 3, p=0.0052, not meeting threshold); 10 mg not superior to placebo on any endpoint

key_safety: Most common adverse events (pooled daridorexant 25 mg, N=618, vs placebo, N=615): headache (5.2% vs 3.7%), somnolence FMQ (7.0% vs 2.8%), and fatigue (2.9% vs 0.7%); dizziness (2.1% vs 1.1%). Psychomotor impairment and CNS-depressant/daytime impairment effects can occur
target_moa: Daridorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist (DORA); its mechanism in insomnia is thought to be through antagonism of orexin 1 (OX1R) and orexin 2 (OX2R) receptors, blocking wake-promoting orexin neuropeptide signaling (Ki = 0.47 and 0.93 nM, respectively)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was held; the drug is not first in its class, trial designs were similar to previously approved products, and the data did not raise unexpected safety or efficacy issues

description.text: Updated Warnings and Precautions and Use in Specific Populations to reflect results of a severe obstructive sleep apnea study

basis.text: The application was reviewed as a standard (not priority) review

summary.text: Idorsia submitted NDA 214985 for daridorexant, an orexin receptor antagonist, for the treatment of insomnia, reviewed as a standard application by the Division of Psychiatry and approved on a first cycle with no advisory committee held. Approval was based on two positive adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (ID-078A301 and ID-078A302). No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designations were applied.

citations.quote: Idorsia submitted a new drug application (NDA) 214985 for daridorexant, an orexin receptor antagonist, for the treatment of insomnia.
The Applicant has provided substantial evidence of effectiveness for daridorexant with two positive adequate and well-controlled trials.
An advisory committee was not held during this marketing application review.
